### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **7** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-record-context`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **48** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/src/utils/namespace-co-owner-names.ts`, `packages/services/service-record-context/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**57** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4fb03ebbfa5a7bb6771a04bc3f41cb370c440a52`.

⛔ **19** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/src/utils/namespace-co-owner-names.ts`, `packages/services/service-record-context/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **10** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **197** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4fb03ebbfa5a7bb6771a04bc3f41cb370c440a52` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `64e40c65818e290efb011da8369d1eacf87cb2cb` — the merge of head `7408543965b4dbbc8e51cf8033e51106d2e2f79d` into base `4fb03ebbfa5a7bb6771a04bc3f41cb370c440a52`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 64e40c65818e290efb011da8369d1eacf87cb2cb && git checkout 64e40c65818e290efb011da8369d1eacf87cb2cb
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4fb03ebbfa5a7bb6771a04bc3f41cb370c440a52 7408543965b4dbbc8e51cf8033e51106d2e2f79d && git checkout -B drift-repro 4fb03ebbfa5a7bb6771a04bc3f41cb370c440a52 && git merge --no-ff 7408543965b4dbbc8e51cf8033e51106d2e2f79d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4fb03ebbfa5a7bb6771a04bc3f41cb370c440a52
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4fb03ebbfa5a7bb6771a04bc3f41cb370c440a52` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7408543965b4dbbc8e51cf8033e51106d2e2f79d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.ai-context-package-scoped-name.ts + packages/core/src/package-scoped-resolution.ts, packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-read.ts, packages/objectql/src/namespace-co-owner-names.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/namespace-co-owner-names.ts, packages/services/service-record-context/src/read-set.ts, packages/services/service-record-context/src/sentences.ts, packages/services/service-record-context/src/record-context-tools.ts, packages/services/service-record-context/src/door.ts, packages/services/service-record-context/src/index.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts, packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts
Security-touching: no
Rule-change-verified: none

**What this record is.** A delta over my full review of head `db7b2e23`, by the same reviewer. That full record was written but never posted (the write was refused by the reviewing session's permission check), so its judgments are restated here and this record stands alone on this head. The full review read card #37216 and every comment, the ADR-0150 addendum of 2026-11-25 with D2 to D6 and D9, ADR-0160 D4 as amended, the PR body, the 26-file list and the net diff against `main` at merge base `057cedfa`. The delta is one commit, `74085439`, over `db7b2e23`: two files, 4 lines added and 3 removed (`.changeset/37216-ai-context-package-scoped.md` and the semantic entry). No other file moved, so every judgment below that is not about those two files is carried from `db7b2e23` unchanged.

### ① Derived judgments

Carried from `db7b2e23`; the delta changes no accept set and no public surface.

1. `PACKAGE_SLOTTED_METADATA_TYPES` gains `ai_context` (published constant). Right: the metadata service's store, its removal and `unregisterPackageWithReport` are generic over the set, so each package's pack keeps its own slot and an uninstall drops one and keeps the other. It also follows that the history and rollback doors take `?package=` for the type (refused `400` before), a widening the PR body does not name, and that an in-process read or removal by name with no package is refused `409` for a name two packages hold.
2. `PACKAGE_SCOPED_TYPES` gains it. Right, and required by item 1: the store's read with no package asks the one rule, which throws for a type outside the list. A by-name read on a registry that cannot read by package answers `501`, as for every listed type; `SchemaRegistry` can.
3. `PACKAGE_SCOPED_READ_TYPES` gains it. Right: `GET /api/v1/meta/ai_context/NAME` with no package, for a name two packages hold, goes from the first match to `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`. No reader passes a package caller for this type yet, so D3 (a) and (c) narrow nothing today.
4. `NAMESPACE_UNIQUE_TYPES` gains it. Right and real at both doors: the predicate reads the `aiContexts` collection, `installPackage` throws `NamespaceNameConflictError` (`422 NAMESPACE_CONFLICT`), and `os validate` prints the same sentence.
5. `get_record_context`: `context` accepts a face, a bare name resolves by D3 for a caller with no package, the several answer lists face and label, a two-holder refusal names each candidate. Right against the addendum's reader 1 and point 2.
6. `@objectstack/service-record-context`: new exports, a changed `selectContextPack` signature and outcome members, `recordContextReadSet().pack` as the face, an optional `RecordContextDoor.packageNamespace`. No importer outside the package in this repository; the changeset states each.

### ② Semver level

- Six packages at `minor` for `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`: met. The changeset carries both declaration lines, the BREAKING banner with a count per narrowing, the one-line fix and one ADR-0087 marker matching the entry's `id`. The delta leaves all of that as it was.
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` holds on the tree: `yes` for the widenings in items 1, 5 and 6, the arm for items 1, 3 and 4. The claim comments on the card (7155305628, 7157432984) still read `no (narrowing)`; the seat reconciles that line. A card that only narrows is `no (narrowing)`; this one is `yes` because it also widens.
- The first BREAKING bullet now reads `422 NAMESPACE_CONFLICT`, as the tree answers.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Carried: the `context` describe still saying "by name" is accepted as routed to #37141; both doors keep `_packageId` through `stripReadDecorations` and the strict parse; the two #32521 fixture changes weaken no assertion (only `ai_context` gets a new file name, `helper.ai-context.yml`); no SQL push-down finding (the diff adds no query).
- First-party counts: objectstack re-measured at `db7b2e23`, one declarer with two packs of different names, 0 on all three arms; the delta touches no declarer. hotcrm at `9b735103` is the dev's reading and was not re-measured (outside the reviewing session's repository scope).
- **Checks on this head.** Read again just before posting, with the head unchanged: all 73 check-runs on `74085439` are concluded, each `success` or `skipped`, none red and none running. Green among them: `Test Core` and its 10 shards, `TypeScript Type Check` with its four lanes, `Lint & Repo Gates` with every Lint lane, `Build Core`, `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, and the UI set (`Type Check UI`, `Test UI` and its 16 shards, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`). So the pins this review cites as running for `ai_context` (the install and `os validate` refusals at `422 NAMESPACE_CONFLICT`, the #32521 host-file cases, the §5 overlay pin, both doors' face cases) ran green on this head. The skipped runs are the opt-in and queue-only jobs. The landing seat still reads the checks itself at the moment it lands.
- The PR author is the fleet bot. No `open_questions` entry in the body.

### ④ Design judgment

**The delta, `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.ai-context-package-scoped-name.ts`.** Holds. The entry's `reason` now reads "refused at install (422 NAMESPACE_CONFLICT, naming every holder) and by os validate". That is the envelope `NamespaceNameConflictError` carries (`code` `NAMESPACE_CONFLICT`, `status` and `httpStatus` `422`), the one the pins assert for the type, and the spelling the sibling entries use. "Naming every holder" is true of the refusal: each conflict lists every other package of the namespace that holds the name. The rewrap of the following sentence changes no word. The changeset's first BREAKING bullet carries the same words, and the PR body's narrowing table was corrected to `422 NAMESPACE_CONFLICT` as well. The three `409` that remain in the entry and the changeset are the by-name read and the `get_record_context` refusals, which do answer `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`.

S1: closed

**Carried from `db7b2e23`, unchanged by the delta.**

- `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`: holds. One row in the list the addendum names, read by its first consumer as item 1 says.
- The entry's disposition (a semantic entry with no conversion and no relevance question), its surface, replacement and acceptance criteria: hold.
- `read-set.ts`: holds. The root narrows first; a face answers its one pack; a face two packs derive is refused naming each holder; a bare name goes to the one rule with no caller package. It is `lookupSkillPrompt`'s order, with one stricter step (two rows of one holder are refused). No arrangement I tried picks silently: an environment pack beside a package pack, a door that cannot place a package, two packages of a shareable namespace, a shared face among several with `context` omitted.
- `sentences.ts`: holds against ADR-0160 D4 step 3 as amended, in en and zh-Hans, with the blank-label fallback pinned.
- `record-context-tools.ts`, `door.ts`, `index.ts`, both MCP doors, and the three list files with the cli header: hold.

**Nits, accepted as they stand (no effect on correctness or the contract).** N1: in `packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts` the new helper sits between `createStdioDataBridge`'s docblock and the function, so the exported function lost its doc comment. N2: two comments outside the diff still count the lists without the pack (`package-slotted-store.ts`, `registry.ts`). N3: the `context` describe, with #37141. N4: the entry's "at once" for `migrateDatabaseLoaderRowPackages` leaves out the `stamp-only` rows that migration does not bind, as the sibling `tool-names-per-namespace` entry does. Each is a follow-up, not a commit on this PR.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

## 维护者速读
- 用户能看到什么变化：两个应用各自带同名资料包时，外部 AI 通过 MCP 读记录资料，可以按「应用前缀-名字」分别选中各自的包；只给名字而两个应用都有这个名字时，会被明确拒绝，并列出每个可选写法。同一个应用里出现第二个同名资料包，安装和 os validate 都会拒绝。
